question_text: Suppose $A = \log_{10} P$, $B = \log_{10} Q$, and $C = \log_{10} R$. Write in terms of $A$, $B$, and $C$:

mark_breakdown.desc: Correct application of product rule to express in terms of $A$ and $B$

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Product property of logarithms: $\log_b(xy) = \log_b x + \log_b y$.
step_by_step: Use the product law: $\log_{10}(PQ) = \log_{10} P + \log_{10} Q$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Multiplying the terms: writing $AB$ instead of $A + B$.

mark_breakdown.desc: Apply product and power rules to separate terms

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Logarithm laws: $\log(xyz) = \log x + \log y + \log z$ and $\log(x^k) = k\log x$.
step_by_step: Bring powers to the front: $2\log_{10} P + \log_{10} Q + \frac{1}{2}\log_{10} R$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Missing the exponent $1/2$ for the square root.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Combine quotient, product, and power rules of logarithms.
